text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Newspaper editorial says President Sali Berisha is trying to repair Albania's image abroad at the OSCE Lisbon summit.
- Albanian authorities and investors are still trying to find the president of the Grunasi company who has allagedly fled the country with $13 million. The firm operated a pyramid scheme.
- Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini's special envoy is meeting Albanian political parties to listen to their views on a new constitution.
- The state will sell shares in strategic businesses.
- Police are watching the apartment of a pyramid scheme organiser who has stopped pay-outs to depositors.
- Albanians are against abolishing the death sentence.
- Albania's government annulled its suspensions of several Albanian soccer federation officials in an attempt to get the country reinstated into international soccer.
- Albanian politicians and 22,000 other public officials will declare their income to a committee set up by parliament.
- Italian police arrested a 26-year old Albanian from the western city of Durres with drugs produced in Albania.
- The government has created a special committee to deal with Albania's aim of signing an agreement with the European Union.
- There have been $228 million in direct foreign investments in Albania since 1991.
